proposition: Let a_0 = 7, a_1 = 33 and a_n = 9*a_(n-1) + (-18)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 25, a_n = 3*3^n + 4*6^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: At n = 0 the closed form gives 7, matching a_0 = 7.
At n = 1 the closed form gives 33, matching a_1 = 33.
The closed form satisfies the recurrence: for every n in [0, 23], f(n+2) = 9*f(n+1) + (-18)*f(n).
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 25 we have n^2 >= 2n.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 25].
There exists an integer n in [1, 25] with n^2 > 25.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 25, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6.
Two base cases plus the recurrence identity give the closed form for every n in [0, 25].
